questions.questionText: An angle measures 38°. What is its complement?
An angle measures 127°. What is its supplement?
Two vertically opposite angles are formed. If one is 74°, what is the other?
questions.explanationText: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so the required angle is 74°.

questions.questionText: Two adjacent angles form a linear pair. One is 115°. Find the other.
Two complementary angles are in the ratio 2:3. Find the larger angle.
questions.explanationText: The 5 ratio parts total 90°, so one part is 18°. The larger angle is 3×18° = 54°.

questions.questionText: Two supplementary angles are in the ratio 4:5. Find the smaller angle.
questions.explanationText: Nine parts equal 180°, so one part is 20°. The smaller angle is 4×20° = 80°.

questions.questionText: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. One corresponding angle is 68°. What is the matching corresponding angle?
questions.explanationText: Corresponding angles between parallel lines are equal, hence 68°.

questions.questionText: A transversal crosses parallel lines. One alternate interior angle is 121°. Find the other alternate interior angle.
questions.explanationText: Alternate interior angles are equal when the lines are parallel.

questions.questionText: Two co-interior angles between parallel lines are supplementary. If one is 47°, find the other.
questions.explanationText: Co-interior angles sum to 180°, so the angle is 180° − 47° = 133°.

questions.questionText: Angles around a point are 95°, 110°, 70°, and x°. Find x.
questions.explanationText: Angles around a point total 360°. Thus x = 360° − 275° = 85°.

questions.questionText: Two angles of a triangle are 65° and 45°. Find the third angle.
An exterior angle of a triangle is 124°. One remote interior angle is 53°. Find the other remote interior angle.
questions.explanationText: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles; 124° − 53° = 71°.

questions.questionText: In an isosceles triangle, the vertex angle is 40°. Find each base angle.
questions.explanationText: The equal base angles share 180° − 40° = 140°, so each is 70°.

questions.questionText: Each angle of an equilateral triangle equals how many degrees?
questions.explanationText: Three equal angles sum to 180°, so each is 60°.

questions.questionText: Which value can be the third side of a triangle whose other sides are 8 cm and 13 cm?
questions.explanationText: Triangle inequality requires 13−8 < x < 13+8, or 5 < x < 21. Only 10 satisfies it.

questions.questionText: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2:3:4. Find the largest angle.
questions.explanationText: Nine ratio parts equal 180°, so each part is 20°. Largest angle = 4×20° = 80°.

questions.questionText: A right triangle has one acute angle of 32°. Find its other acute angle.
questions.explanationText: The two acute angles in a right triangle sum to 90°; 90° − 32° = 58°.

questions.questionText: In an isosceles triangle, one base angle is 72°. Find the vertex angle.
questions.explanationText: The base angles are both 72°, leaving 180° − 144° = 36°.

questions.questionText: A triangle has sides 7 cm, 9 cm, and 12 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanationText: Perimeter is the sum of sides: 7 + 9 + 12 = 28 cm.

questions.questionText: The exterior angle at a vertex of an equilateral triangle is what measure?
questions.explanationText: The exterior angle is supplementary to the 60° interior angle: 180° − 60° = 120°.

questions.questionText: In a right triangle, the perpendicular sides are 3 m and 4 m. Find the hypotenuse.

Two similar triangles have corresponding sides in the ratio 3:5. If a side of the smaller triangle is 12 cm, find the corresponding larger side.
The areas of two similar triangles are in the ratio 9:16. What is the ratio of corresponding sides?
questions.explanationText: The side ratio is the square root of the area ratio: √9:√16 = 3:4.

questions.questionText: A 6 cm side in one triangle corresponds to a 15 cm side in a similar triangle. If another side is 10 cm in the first, find its counterpart.
questions.explanationText: Scale factor = 15/6 = 2.5, so the side is 10×2.5 = 25 cm.

questions.questionText: The medians of a triangle meet at its centroid. In what ratio does the centroid divide each median, measured from the vertex?
questions.explanationText: The centroid divides every median in the ratio 2:1 from the vertex.

questions.questionText: A median is 18 cm long. Find the distance from the vertex to the centroid.
questions.explanationText: The vertex-to-centroid portion is 2/3 of the median: 2×18/3 = 12 cm.

questions.questionText: Two triangles have all three corresponding sides equal. Which congruence rule applies?
questions.explanationText: Equality of all three corresponding sides is the SSS congruence condition.

questions.questionText: Two right triangles have equal hypotenuses and one corresponding side equal. Which congruence rule applies?
questions.explanationText: Right angle, hypotenuse, and one side establish RHS congruence.

questions.questionText: An angle bisector divides the opposite side into segments 6 cm and 9 cm. What is the ratio of the adjacent sides?
questions.explanationText: By the angle-bisector theorem, adjacent sides are in the ratio 6:9 = 2:3.

questions.questionText: In similar triangles, corresponding altitudes are 8 cm and 14 cm. What is the ratio of their areas?
questions.explanationText: Linear ratio is 8:14 = 4:7; area ratio is 4²:7² = 16:49.

questions.questionText: A triangle has base 12 cm. A similar triangle has twice every linear dimension. What is the ratio of their perimeters, smaller to larger?
questions.explanationText: Perimeters scale linearly, so doubling all sides gives ratio 1:2.

questions.questionText: A triangle and a parallelogram stand on the same base and between the same parallels. If the triangle area is 45 cm², find the parallelogram area.
questions.explanationText: The parallelogram has twice the area of the triangle: 2×45 = 90 cm².

questions.questionText: A triangular field has sides 15 m, 20 m, and 25 m. Find its area.
questions.explanationText: The sides form a right triangle. Area = 1/2×15×20 = 150 m².

questions.explanationText: A radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so the angle is 90°.

questions.questionText: An angle subtended by a diameter at a point on the circle is how many degrees?
questions.explanationText: An angle in a semicircle is a right angle, equal to 90°.

questions.questionText: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary. If one is 108°, find the opposite angle.
Two equal chords of the same circle subtend central angles. If one angle is 76°, find the other.
questions.explanationText: Equal chords of a circle subtend equal angles at the centre.

questions.questionText: A chord is 24 cm long and is 5 cm from the centre. Find the radius.
questions.explanationText: The perpendicular bisects the chord. Radius = √(12²+5²) = 13 cm.

questions.questionText: A circle has radius 10 cm. A chord is 16 cm long. Find the perpendicular distance from the centre to the chord.
The angle at the centre standing on an arc is 100°. What is the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc?
questions.explanationText: The central angle is twice the inscribed angle; 100°/2 = 50°.

questions.questionText: An inscribed angle standing on an arc is 42°. Find the central angle on the same arc.
questions.explanationText: The central angle is twice the inscribed angle: 2×42° = 84°.

questions.questionText: Two tangents are drawn from the same external point. One tangent length is 15 cm. Find the other.
questions.explanationText: Tangents from the same external point to a circle are equal.

questions.questionText: A circle has diameter 26 cm. What is its radius?
questions.explanationText: Radius is half the diameter: 26/2 = 13 cm.

questions.questionText: A circle of radius 7 cm is inscribed in a square. Find the square area. Use π = 22/7.
questions.explanationText: The square side equals the diameter, 14 cm. Area = 14² = 196 cm².

questions.questionText: A circle of radius 7 cm is inscribed in a square. Find the area inside the square but outside the circle. Use π = 22/7.
questions.explanationText: Square area = 14² = 196; circle area = 154. Difference = 42 cm².

questions.questionText: A square of side 14 cm contains a circular cut-out of radius 3.5 cm. Find the remaining area. Use π = 22/7.
Two concentric circles have radii 14 cm and 7 cm. Find the annulus area. Use π = 22/7.
A square is inscribed in a circle of radius 5√2 cm. Find the square side.
questions.explanationText: The square diagonal equals diameter = 10√2. Side = diagonal/√2 = 10 cm.

questions.questionText: A rectangle 20 cm by 14 cm has a semicircle of diameter 14 cm attached externally along one shorter side. Find the total area. Use π = 22/7.
questions.explanationText: Rectangle area = 280; semicircle area = 1/2×22/7×7² = 77. Total = 357 cm².

questions.questionText: A rectangle 20 cm by 14 cm has a semicircle of diameter 14 cm attached externally. Find its outer perimeter. Use π = 22/7.
questions.explanationText: Outer perimeter = two lengths + one width + semicircular arc = 40+14+22 = 76 cm.

questions.questionText: A circular garden has radius 14 m. A square lawn of side 14 m lies inside it. Find the circle area minus square area. Use π = 22/7.
questions.explanationText: Circle area = 616; square area = 196; difference = 420 m².

questions.questionText: A 30 cm by 20 cm sheet has a 10 cm by 8 cm rectangle removed. Find the remaining area.
A 24 cm square is cut along a diagonal into two equal triangles. Find the area of each triangle.
questions.explanationText: Square area = 24² = 576; each triangle is half, or 288 cm².

questions.questionText: A rectangular garden is 30 m by 20 m. A 2 m wide path is built outside it. Find the path area.
questions.explanationText: Outer dimensions are 34 m by 24 m. Path area = 34×24 − 30×20 = 816−600 = 216 m².

questions.questionText: A square plot has side 20 m. A 2 m wide path runs inside along all edges. Find the path area.
questions.explanationText: Inner square side = 20−4 = 16 m. Path area = 20²−16² = 144 m².

questions.questionText: A circular garden of radius 14 m has a 7 m wide outer path. Find the path area. Use π = 22/7.
questions.explanationText: Outer radius = 21 m. Path area = π(21²−14²)=22/7×245=770 m².

questions.questionText: A rectangular picture is 24 cm by 18 cm and has a uniform 2 cm frame outside. Find the frame area.
A square courtyard has outer side 30 m and an inner grass square of side 24 m. Find the paved border area.
A 40 m by 25 m field has a 3 m wide path inside. Find the remaining inner area.
questions.explanationText: Inner dimensions = 34×19, so remaining area = 646 m².

questions.questionText: A circular track has outer radius 21 m and inner radius 14 m. Find its area. Use π = 22/7.
A 50 m by 30 m plot has a 5 m wide road outside. Find the road area.
A square lawn of side 18 m has a 1 m border outside. Find the border area.
questions.explanationText: Outer side = 20 m. Border area = 20²−18² = 76 m².

questions.questionText: A circular pond of diameter 28 m has a 3.5 m outer walkway. Find walkway area. Use π = 22/7.
questions.explanationText: Inner radius = 14; outer radius = 17.5. Area = 22/7(17.5²−14²) = 346.5 m².

questions.explanationText: It is a right triangle with base 6 and height 8. Area = 1/2×6×8 = 24 square units.

questions.questionText: What is the slope of a horizontal line?

questions.questionText: What is the slope of a vertical line?

questions.questionText: Points (1,2), (3,6), and (5,10) are collinear. What is their common slope?
questions.explanationText: Slope from the first to second is (6−2)/(3−1)=2, matching the other pair.

questions.explanationText: A pyramid has one-third the volume of the corresponding prism: 750/3 = 250 cm³.

A solid is formed by joining two cubes of edge 4 cm face to face. Find its volume.
questions.explanationText: Each cube volume is 4³=64; total = 2×64 = 128 cm³.

A hemisphere of radius 7 cm is attached to the base of a cone with the same radius and height 12 cm. Find total volume. Use π = 22/7. Give two decimals.
questions.explanationText: Hemisphere volume = 718.67 and cone volume = 616; total = 1334.67 cm³.

Two cubes have edges in ratio 2:3. Find their volume ratio.
questions.explanationText: Volumes scale as cube of edge ratio: 2³:3³ = 8:27.

questions.questionText: Two spheres have radii in ratio 3:5. Find their surface-area ratio.
questions.explanationText: Surface areas scale as r², so ratio = 3²:5² = 9:25.

questions.questionText: Two similar cones have heights in ratio 2:5. Find their volume ratio.
questions.explanationText: All linear dimensions scale 2:5, so volumes scale 2³:5³ = 8:125.

questions.questionText: A cylinder and cone have equal base and height. What is the volume ratio cylinder:cone?
questions.explanationText: Cylinder volume is πr²h and cone volume is one-third of that, giving 3:1.

questions.questionText: A metal cuboid 8 cm × 6 cm × 3 cm is melted into cubes of edge 2 cm. How many cubes form?
questions.explanationText: Cuboid volume = 144 cm³; small cube volume = 8 cm³; number = 18.

questions.questionText: A sphere of radius 3 cm is recast into a cylinder of radius 3 cm. Find cylinder height.
questions.explanationText: Equate volumes: 4/3π×3³ = π×3²×h, so h = 4 cm.

questions.questionText: The surface areas of two cubes are in ratio 25:49. Find their edge ratio.
questions.explanationText: Surface area scales with edge², so edge ratio = √25:√49 = 5:7.

questions.questionText: A cube is cut into 64 equal smaller cubes. If the original edge is 12 cm, find each small edge.
questions.explanationText: 64 = 4³, so each edge is divided by 4: 12/4 = 3 cm.

questions.questionText: A cubical tank has side 2 m. What is its capacity in litres?
questions.explanationText: Volume = 2³=8 m³. Since 1 m³=1000 L, capacity = 8000 L.

questions.questionText: A tank measures 2.5 m × 2 m × 1.5 m. Find its capacity in litres.
How many litres are in 350000 cm³?
Convert 4.2 m³ to litres.
A box 60 cm × 40 cm × 30 cm is packed with cubes of side 10 cm. How many fit exactly?
How many 5 cm cubes fit in a cuboid 25 cm × 20 cm × 15 cm?
A hectare equals how many square metres?
Convert 25000 cm² to m².
A 1.2 m cube has volume how many cubic centimetres?
A container holds 2.75 litres. Express this in cubic centimetres.
Two similar squares have side ratio 3:7. Find their area ratio.
questions.explanationText: Area ratio is square of side ratio: 9:49.

questions.questionText: Two similar solids have linear ratio 4:5. Find their volume ratio.
A map scale is 1:5000. A rectangular plot measures 4 cm by 3 cm on the map. Find actual area in m².
questions.explanationText: Actual dimensions are 200 m and 150 m. Area = 30,000 m².

questions.questionText: A model cube has edge 4 cm; the real cube has edge 2 m. Find model:real volume ratio.
questions.explanationText: Convert 2 m to 200 cm. Edge ratio 1:50, volume ratio = 1:125000.

questions.questionText: Corresponding sides of similar rectangles are in ratio 2:3. If smaller area is 40 cm², find larger area.
A photograph is enlarged so every linear dimension increases by 50%. By what factor does its area increase?
The radius of a sphere doubles. By what factor does its volume increase?
questions.explanationText: Sphere volume scales as r³; doubling gives 2³ = 8.

questions.questionText: The edge of a cube is reduced to half. What fraction of the original surface area remains?
questions.explanationText: Surface area scales with edge², so (1/2)² = 1/4.

questions.questionText: A triangle is scaled by factor 3. If its original area is 18 cm², find new area.
A cylinder’s radius and height are both tripled. By what factor does volume increase?
A ladder 13 m long rests against a wall with its foot 5 m away. How high does it reach?
A rectangular park 80 m by 60 m has a straight diagonal path. Find its length.
A cylindrical water tank of radius 1.4 m and height 2.5 m holds how many litres? Use π = 22/7.
A hemispherical dome has radius 7 m. Find the exterior curved area to paint. Use π = 22/7.
A closed cubical box of edge 5 m is painted outside at ₹40 per m². Find cost.
A cylindrical can of radius 7 cm and height 20 cm is open at the top. Find sheet area. Use π = 22/7.
A conical tent has radius 7 m and slant height 25 m. Find canvas area excluding the base. Use π = 22/7.
A 100 m by 60 m field is divided by a path 4 m wide running across the full 60 m width. Find path area.
A square metal plate of side 20 cm has four corner squares of side 2 cm removed. Find remaining area.
questions.explanationText: Original area 400; removed area 4×4=16; remaining = 384 cm².

questions.questionText: A pipe has inner radius 3 cm, outer radius 5 cm, and length 100 cm. Find material volume using π = 3.14.
A square has the same area as a rectangle 32 cm by 18 cm. Find the square side.
questions.explanationText: Rectangle area = 576 cm²; square side = √576 = 24 cm.

questions.questionText: A circle has area 616 cm². Find its radius using π = 22/7.
A cylinder has volume 2464 cm³ and height 16 cm. Find its radius using π = 22/7.
A cone has volume 1232 cm³ and radius 7 cm. Find its height using π = 22/7.
A cube has total surface area 864 cm². Find its edge.
A sphere has surface area 616 cm². Find its radius using π = 22/7.
A rectangular field has perimeter 180 m and length 55 m. Find its area.
An annulus has outer radius 14 cm and area 462 cm². Find inner radius using π = 22/7.
questions.explanationText: 462 = π(196−r²). Thus 147=196−r², so r²=49 and r=7 cm.

questions.questionText: A regular polygon has each interior angle 150°. How many sides does it have?
A cuboid has volume 960 cm³, length 12 cm, and breadth 8 cm. Find height.
A regular polygon has 44 diagonals. How many sides does it have?
A rectangle has diagonal 25 cm and width 15 cm. Find its area.
A rhombus has area 240 cm² and one diagonal 16 cm. Find its perimeter.
questions.explanationText: Other diagonal = 2×240/16=30. Half-diagonals 8 and 15 give side 17, so perimeter=4×17=68 cm.

questions.questionText: A cylindrical tank of radius 7 m is filled to a depth of 3 m. How many litres of water does it contain? Use π = 22/7.
A cube is cut into 125 equal cubes. The total surface area of all small cubes is what multiple of the original cube’s surface area?
questions.explanationText: 125=5³, so each edge is 1/5. Total surface area factor = 125×(1/5)² = 5.

questions.questionText: A cone and a hemisphere have equal radii and equal volumes. If the cone height is h and radius is r, find h:r.
A 14 m radius circular garden is surrounded by a path whose area equals the garden area. Find the outer radius.
questions.explanationText: π(R²−14²)=π14², so R²=2×14² and R=14√2 m.

questions.questionText: A solid sphere fits exactly inside a cube of edge 14 cm. What fraction of the cube volume is occupied by the sphere? Use π = 22/7.
A square and a circle have equal perimeters. If the square side is 11 cm, find the circle radius using π = 22/7.
questions.explanationText: Square perimeter=44. Set 2πr=44, so r=44×7/44=7 cm.

questions.questionText: A closed cylinder has fixed volume. If its radius is doubled while volume stays constant, the height becomes what fraction of its original value?
questions.explanationText: V=πr²h. Doubling r multiplies r² by 4, so h must become one-fourth.
